originality.rationale: Sontag 2026 proves no-connectivity global attraction for undelayed systems (Theorem 3) and separate delayed global attraction under (A2)-(A3) (Theorem 6). The new claim simultaneously admits arbitrarily delayed dynamics and reducible graphs whenever a positive equilibrium exists, with an explicit history-based decay exponent. Literature and indexed record comparisons identified no stronger direct assertion; generic-delay corollary priority remains a risk.

value.rationale: The source treats arbitrary-delay global attraction only under strongly connected, nondegenerate network assumptions while its topology-free result has no delays. A single reducible network can contain feedback subsystems and downstream species, so proving unconditional global convergence for arbitrary fixed delays from all positive histories, with an explicit computable rate, has model-design relevance and changes the applicable class rather than merely adjusting a constant. The result distinguishes a meaningful stability mechanism from known local stability.
